name: Iyawo Sequence — Geneware Living Textile Gallery
creator: Folashade Iyawo-Petersen, Shelf-born bioengineer and textile artist
description: A gallery exhibition of twenty-three living fabric works, each engineered from geneware silk-producing organisms whose color and texture shift in response to atmospheric data piped in from specific Meridian 88 districts — air quality, noise levels, ambient BCI traffic density, recorded emotional valence from public neural feeds. A piece titled 'Ochota, 3am' shifts through a precise and ugly palette of grey-brown and pale amber; 'Spire Atrium Noon' blazes in sustained gold. The fabrics breathe visibly.
medium: physical / bioart / geneware organism / living textile
cultural_impact: The exhibition's data-sourcing made inequality in Meridian 88 viscerally legible in a way statistics could not; 'Ochota, 3am' became a widely reproduced image in Shelf advocacy materials.
controversy: Axiom Consolidated's environmental monitoring division disputed the accuracy of the atmospheric data feeds, alleging the artist had manipulated inputs to exaggerate disparities. Independent verification confirmed the data was unaltered.
story_hooks: Iyawo-Petersen is approached to create a private commission for a Spire family who want a living textile that displays data from their own estate — she agrees, but quietly sources data from the Shelf workers who service the building instead.
One of the gallery pieces begins displaying data that doesn't match any known Meridian 88 district; the artist has no explanation for what it is responding to.

A Shelf community council wants to acquire 'Ochota, 3am' permanently as a neighborhood artifact, but the organism requires expensive maintenance they can't afford — and a Tier 4 collector is offering to buy it.
